long_biography.plain_text:
Sabancı Çetindoğan studied business at Richmond College in London before spending roughly two decades in textile companies linked to her family’s industrial group. In 1999, she and her husband, Cengiz Çetindoğan, founded Demsa, developing it around international fashion labels, department-store partnerships and multi-brand retail in Turkey.

She remains Demsa’s deputy chair as the group operates luxury retail, hospitality and property businesses. Her later ventures include Onkim, a stem-cell technology company, and Shopsa, an online marketplace designed to connect women producers and cooperatives with customers. She also founded Turkey One, an association focused on cultural preservation and dialogue between generations.
